title: Graceful stream drain and client-cancel sweep for OpenAI adapter
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a soft stream drain and periodic client-cancel sweep to reduce duplicate tool/function calls during abrupt disconnects. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI-compatible abort semantics. Config flags introduced: openai.compat.soft_stream_drain_ms, openai.compat.client_cancel_sweep_ms.
description: Motivation: We observe duplicated tool/function calls and flapping state when clients disconnect abruptly and immediately reconnect with a new connection that races with in-flight server-side commits. This is particularly visible for OpenAI-compatible clients that expect the same abort semantics but do not always close cleanly. This PR adds a graceful 'soft drain' window on server-side connection close plus a periodic client-cancel sweep that reconciles lingering in-flight operations so downstream tool invocations are not executed twice. Scope: 1) soft drain: on receipt of a client disconnect or abort event we transition the server stream into DRAINING for a configurable window (default 250ms) during which we continue to stream buffered tokens but suppress duplicate tool invocation deliveries and allow short-lived reconnects to reattach. 2) client-cancel sweep: a background reconciler periodically queries active session leases and issues idempotent cancel confirmations for sessions with ambiguous finalization to prevent orphaned toolcalls. 3) structured-output fences: we tighten fences for partial-structured outputs so the adapter will only emit toolcall events when a complete fence sequence is closed, reducing partial-toolcall noise. 4) OpenAI-compat handshake: add a compatibility handshake flag that keeps legacy abort semantics unless the client opts into 'soft_drain_v1' to preserve behavior for older clients. Checklist: - [x] Design docs and protocol notes (lease_handshake.md) - [x] Implementation of drain and sweep logic - [x] Unit tests for idempotency and fence handling - [x] Integration test for reconnects and short lived disconnects - [x] Metrics and observability (streaming_metrics.prom) - [x] Example in SDK python for users to opt into new behavior Commits summary: initial spike: add soft drain state machine and handshake flag; add drain policy and reconciliation loop; add structured-output fence guard; tests and flaky-test fixes; docs and changelog. The changes are intentionally conservative and behind config flags with defaults set to maintain existing production behavior. Related work: addresses regression described in ENG-3124 and follows up on discussion in ENG-3180. Implementation notes: soft drain is implemented as a state transition with an adjustable deadline; during DRAINING we mark any newly-observed toolcall candidates as "suppressed-pending" and buffer an idempotency token. If the client reconnects and reattaches with the same session token within the window we clear suppression and deliver only the first delivery. The client-cancel sweep reconciler uses a bounded parallel worker pool and respects existing rate limits. A new metric streaming.soft_drain_suppressed_total was added to help evaluate impact. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves prior semantics; opt-in via openai.compat.soft_stream_drain_v1=true flips to the new behavior. Testing notes: added soft_cancel_test.go with deterministic fake clocks to validate timing edge cases. Integration pipeline initially failed due to flaky stream_integration_test (seed-dependent); fixed by stabilizing test seeding and reducing timeouts. CI: all checks passed on final run. Merge strategy: squash and merge. Merge notes: no migration required, behavior behind flags, no changes to API contracts beyond documented flags.
review_comments: Evan Lewis: Please add a unit test that simulates second connection racing in with delayed backend commit. The new state machine looks good but we need explicit coverage.
Maya Chen (author): Added determinisitc race test and a fake commit hook to validate suppression semantics. See soft_cancel_test.go commit.
Priya Nair: We should ensure metrics have tags for tenant and model to help analysis in multi-tenant clusters. Also note potential perf impact of sweep; please add a token bucket limiter.
Maya Chen (author): Added tenant/model labels to streaming.soft_drain_suppressed_total and a configurable sweep_rate_limit in drain_policy.go. Benchmarks show <2% CPU for default settings.
Lukas Müller: Docs look good. One nit: callout in changelog should advise users how to opt-out, otherwise they may be surprised. Approving after the changelog entry is clarified.
Maya Chen (author): Clarified changelog and added an example snippet in docs/openai_compat/streaming-behavior.md. CI green, ready to merge.
notes: This PR reduces duplicate tool invocations during abrupt disconnects by combining a short server-side soft drain with a background cancel sweep. Feature gated and backward compatible. Observability added to measure the real-world effect before enabling platform-wide.
